12 : 252: I bear witness that I heard the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) say: "Whoever wears silk will be forbidden to wear it in the Hereafter."
12 : 253: Narrated Abu Sa'id al-Khudri: The Prophet ﷺ said: "Whoever wears silk in this world will not wear it in the Hereafter, and if he enters Paradise, the people of Paradise will wear it, but he will not wear it."
0: Narrated Anas: Fatimah wept for the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, saying: "O my father, how near he is to his Lord! O my father, to Jibril we announce his death! O my father, the Garden of Paradise is his abode!"
12 : 325: Narrated 'Aishah: A young girl from among the Ansar got married, and she fell ill, so her hair fell out. They wanted to attach false hair to it, so they asked the Messenger of Allah ﷺ about that. He cursed the one who attaches false hair and the one who has it attached.
12 : 254: Narrated 'Ali ibn Abi Talib: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) forbade the gold ring, Al-Qassiy (a type of silk garment), and Al-Mithara (a silk cushion or saddle-cloth used for riding).
2 : 499: The Prophet ﷺ was brought some dates from charity, so I took a date and put it in my mouth, whereupon he took it out along with my saliva and put it back among the dates. It was said to him: "O Messenger of Allah, what harm would it have been for you had you left this date with this child?" He said: "We, the family of Muhammad, charity is not lawful for us."
12 : 196: Narrated Abu Musa Al-Ash'ari: When the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) sent me and Mu'adh ibn Jabal to Yemen, he commanded us that each of us should stay near the other, and he said to us: "Make things easy and do not make them difficult, give glad tidings and do not repel people." When we got up to leave, we said: "O Messenger of Allah, give us a ruling concerning two drinks that we used to make: Al-Bit', made from honey, which is left to ferment until it becomes strong, and Al-Mizr, made from barley and corn (or sorghum), which is left to ferment until it becomes strong." The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) had been given comprehensiveness of speech and its most decisive expressions, so he (ﷺ) said: "Every intoxicant that intoxicates and keeps one away from the prayer is forbidden for you."
12 : 255: Narrated Ibn 'Umar: 'Umar bin Al-Khattab saw a garment of silk (Hullah Siyara) at the door of the mosque and said, "O Messenger of Allah, if only you would buy this and wear it on Friday and when delegations come to you." The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said, "This is only worn by one who has no share in the Hereafter." Then some garments of that kind were brought to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), and he gave one of them to 'Umar bin Al-Khattab. 'Umar said, "O Messenger of Allah, you have clothed me with it, while you said what you said about the garment of 'Utarid?" The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said, "I did not give it to you to wear it." So 'Umar gave it to a brother of his who was a polytheist in Makkah.
12 : 330: Narrated Al-Bara': Whenever the Messenger of Allah ﷺ lay down to sleep, he would place his right hand under his right cheek, then say: "O Allah, protect me from Your punishment on the Day You resurrect Your servants."
12 : 328: Narrated Abu Musa: A house in Madinah burned down upon its occupants at night. When the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) was told of what had befallen them, he said: "Verily, this fire is your enemy, so when you go to sleep, extinguish it."
12 : 329: Narrated Abu Hurayrah: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Whoever goes to sleep with grease (traces of food) on his hand, and something afflicts him, let him blame no one but himself."
12 : 326: Narrated Jabir bin 'Abdullah: I heard the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) saying: "When you hear the barking of dogs or the braying of donkeys at night, seek refuge in Allah, for they see what you do not see. Reduce going out when the night has settled, for Allah, Mighty and Sublime, spreads forth from His creation during the night whatever He wills. Close the doors and mention the name of Allah over them, for Satan does not open a door that has been closed with the name of Allah mentioned over it. Cover the jars, turn over the vessels, and tie up the waterskins."
12 : 327: Narrated Ibn 'Abbas: A mouse came and took hold of a wick, dragging it along, and a slave-girl went to drive it away. The Prophet (ﷺ) said: "Leave it." He said: So it came with it and dropped it before the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) on the small mat upon which he was sitting, and it burned a spot the size of a dirham. He (ﷺ) then said: "When you go to sleep, put out your lamps, for indeed Satan directs creatures like this one to something like this, and it will burn you."
13 : 110: Narrated 'Abdullah ibn Zam'ah: that he heard the Prophet ﷺ say in his sermon, while mentioning the she-camel and the one who slaughtered her: "When the most wretched of them arose [to kill her], there arose for her a violent man, mighty and unassailable among his people, like Abu Zam'ah."
13 : 182: Narrated Buraydah: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Whoever plays with dice (Nard) is like one who dips his hand in the flesh and blood of a pig."
13 : 481: Narrated Abu Hurayrah: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "There is no 'Adwa (contagion) and no Tiyarah (belief in bad omens), and Al-Fa'l (good omen) pleases me."
13 : 482: Narrated Abu Hurairah: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "There is no 'Adwa (contagion, i.e., no disease is transmitted without Allah's permission)."
13 : 183:
Narrated Abu Hurayrah: The Prophet ﷺ saw a man chasing a pigeon, and he said: "A devil chasing a she-devil."

Abu Hatim said: The one who plays with pigeons does not go beyond his play except that it leads him into what Allah, Mighty and Sublime, dislikes, and the one who commits what Allah dislikes is a sinner (disobedient), and it is permissible to call the disobedient one a devil, even though he is one of the children of Adam. Allah, the Exalted, has said: "devils among mankind and jinn," thus naming the disobedient among both of them devils. As for his ﷺ applying the name "devil" to the pigeon, this is by association, and because the act arising from the disobedient one through his playing with it extended to it as well.
13 : 185: Narrated 'Aishah: There was a girl from the Ansar under my care, and I arranged her marriage. She said: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, entered upon me on the day of her wedding, but he did not hear any singing or playing. So he said: "O 'Aishah, did you not sing for her? Why do you not sing for her?" Then he said: "Indeed, this tribe of the Ansar love singing."
13 : 186: Narrated 'Aishah: Abu Bakr entered upon her while two young girls were with her, singing with tambourines and singing about the days [of battle] of the two tribes (Bu'ath), while the Messenger of Allah ﷺ was covering himself with his garment. Abu Bakr rebuked them, but the Messenger of Allah ﷺ uncovered his face and said: "Leave them alone, O Abu Bakr, for these are the days of Eid." 'Aishah said: And when the delegation of the Abyssinians came to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, they stood up playing in the mosque, and I saw the Messenger of Allah ﷺ shielding me with his cloak while I watched them playing in the mosque, until I was the one who grew tired. So estimate accordingly the measure of a young girl who is eager for amusement.
13 : 480: Narrated Abu Sa'eed Al-Khudri: We stopped at a certain place, and a woman came to us and said, "The chief of this settlement has been stung, and is there any among you who can perform a charm (Ruqyah)?" A man from among us got up and went with her, though we did not think he knew how to perform any charm well. He recited the Fatihah over him and he recovered, so they gave him some sheep and gave him milk to drink. I said, "Do not touch them until we come, until we come to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ)." So we came to the Prophet (ﷺ) and mentioned that to him, and he said, "How did he know that it was a Ruqyah? Divide (the sheep) and give me a share along with you."
14 : 311: We did not know what to say when we sat in the prayer, until he taught us. He said: "Say: 'At-Tahiyyatu lillahi wa as-Salawatu wa at-Tayyibat, as-Salamu 'alayka ayyuha an-Nabiyyu wa rahmatullahi wa barakatuh, as-Salamu 'alayna wa 'ala 'ibadillahi as-salihin, ash-hadu an la ilaha illallahu wahdahu la sharika lahu, wa ash-hadu anna Muhammadan 'abduhu wa rasuluh (All compliments are due to Allah, and all prayers and good deeds. Peace be upon you, O Prophet, and the mercy of Allah and His blessings. Peace be upon us and upon the righteous servants of Allah. I bear witness that there is no god but Allah, alone, with no partner, and I bear witness that Muhammad is His servant and His Messenger).'"
14 : 585: Narrated 'Aishah: She heard the Prophet (ﷺ), while she was leaning him against her chest before he died, listening closely to him, saying: "O Allah, forgive me, have mercy on me, and join me with the Highest Companions."
14 : 497: Narrated Abu Al-'Ala' Yazid ibn 'Abdullah ibn Ash-Shikhkhir: We were at Al-Mirbad when I saw a man with disheveled hair, holding a piece of leather in his hand. We said to him, "It seems you are a man from the desert people." He said, "Yes." So we said to him, "Give us this piece of leather that is in your hand." We took it and read what was written on it, and it read: "From Muhammad, the Messenger of Allah, to the Banu Zuhayr: Give the fifth (khumus) of the spoils, and the share of the Prophet and the Safiyy, and you shall be safe under the protection of Allah and the protection of His Messenger." We asked him, "Who wrote this for you?" He said, "The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him."
14 : 586: Narrated Ibn 'Abbas and 'Aishah: When death approached the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), he began to put a garment over his face, and when he felt distressed by it, he would remove it from his face, saying: "May the curse of Allah be upon the Jews and the Christians, for they took the graves of their prophets as places of worship." 'Aishah said: He was warning [his Ummah] against doing the like of what they did.
14 : 517: Narrated Tariq ibn 'Abdullah al-Muharibi: I saw the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) in the market of Dhu al-Majaz, wearing a red cloak, saying: "O people, say 'There is no god but Allah' and you will succeed." Meanwhile, a man was following him, throwing stones at him, until he had drawn blood from his heels and ankles, saying: "O people, do not obey him, for he is a liar." I asked, "Who is this?" It was said, "This is the boy of the Banu 'Abd al-Muttalib." I asked, "Then who is this man following him and throwing stones at him?" He said, "This is 'Abd al-'Uzza, Abu Lahab."
14 : 587: Narrated Anas ibn Malik: While the Muslims were performing the Fajr prayer on Monday, with Abu Bakr leading them in prayer, nothing surprised them more than the appearance of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), who had lifted the curtain of Aisha's chamber. He looked at them as they stood in rows in their prayer, then he smiled and laughed. Abu Bakr stepped back on his heels to join the row, thinking that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) intended to come out to lead the prayer. Anas said: The Muslims were about to be distracted from their prayer out of joy at seeing the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), but the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) gestured to them to complete their prayer. Then he entered the chamber and drew the curtain between himself and them. And the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) passed away that very day.
13 : 54: Narrated Abu Sa'eed al-Khudri: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ went out on the day of Adha or Fitr to the place of prayer. He prayed, then finished, then stood up and admonished the people and commanded them to give charity. He said: "O people, give charity." Then he left and passed by the women, and said: "O women, give charity, for indeed I have seen that you are the majority of the inhabitants of the Fire." They said: "Why is that, O Messenger of Allah?" He said: "You curse frequently and are ungrateful to your husbands. I have not seen any deficient in intelligence and religion more able to overcome the mind of a resolute man than one of you, O women." They said to him: "What is the deficiency in our religion and intelligence, O Messenger of Allah?" He said: "Is not the testimony of a woman equal to half the testimony of a man?" They said: "Yes." He said: "That is the deficiency in her intelligence. And is it not the case that when a woman menstruates, she does not pray and does not fast?" They said: "Yes." He said: "That is the deficiency in her religion."
14 : 516: Narrated 'Aishah: She said to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ): "Did there come upon you a day more severe than the day of Uhud?" He said: "I certainly suffered from your people, and the severest of what I suffered from them was on the day of 'Aqabah, when I presented myself to Ibn 'Abd Yalail ibn 'Abd Kulal, and he did not respond to what I wanted. So I went away, distressed, going on my way, and I raised my head, and there I saw a cloud shading me. I looked, and there was Jibril, peace be upon him, in it. He called out to me and said: 'Indeed, Allah has heard what your people said to you and how they responded to you, and He has sent to you the Angel of the Mountains so that you may command him as you wish concerning them.' He said: Then the Angel of the Mountains called out to me and greeted me, then said: 'O Muhammad, indeed Allah has heard what your people said to you, and I am the Angel of the Mountains, and your Lord has sent me to you so that you may command me as you wish. If you wish, I will bring together the two mountains upon them.'" The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Rather, I hope that Allah will bring forth from their loins those who will worship Allah alone, not associating anything with Him."
14 : 84: Narrated Abu Hurairah: The Prophet ﷺ said: "Ibrahim circumcised himself with an adze when he was one hundred and twenty years old, and he lived for eighty years after that."
14 : 83: Narrated Ibn 'Umar: In the year of the expedition to Tabuk, the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) stopped at Al-Hijr, near the dwellings of Thamud. The people drew water from the wells from which Thamud used to drink, and they set up their cooking pots and kneaded their dough with it. The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Pour out the pots and feed the dough to the camels." Then he moved on until he stopped at the place from which the she-camel used to drink, and he said: "Do not enter upon these people who were punished, lest what befell them befall you as well."
15 : 33: Narrated Ibn 'Umar: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "This matter (authority) will remain with the Quraysh as long as two people remain among mankind."
14 : 592:
Narrated Anas: When the distress overwhelmed the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), his head was in Fatimah's lap. Fatimah said, "O the distress, for your distress today, O my father!" So the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) raised his head and said, "There will be no distress upon your father after today, O Fatimah." When he passed away, Fatimah said, "O my father, he has answered a Lord Who called him. O my father, how close he now is to his Lord! O my father, to the Garden of Firdaws is his abode. O my father, to Jibril do we announce his death."

Anas said: When we had buried him, I passed by the dwelling of Fatimah, and she said, "O Anas, did your hearts allow you to cast dust upon the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ)?"
15 : 43: Narrated Jabir ibn Samurah: I heard the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) say: "There will be twelve caliphs after me, all of them from Quraysh." When he returned to his house, Quraysh came to him and asked: "Then what will be?" He said: "Then there will be chaos (al-Harj)."
15 : 42: Narrated Abu Hurayrah: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "There will be after me leaders (khulafa') who act according to what they know and do what they are commanded. Then there will come after them leaders who act according to what they do not know and do what they are not commanded. Whoever disapproves of them is absolved, but whoever is pleased and follows..."
15 : 188:
Ibn Shihab said: Salim said: "I heard Ibn 'Umar say: 'After that, the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) and Ubayy ibn Ka'b went to the palm grove where Ibn Sayyad was. When the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) entered the palm grove, he began to conceal himself behind the trunks of the palm trees, wishing to hear something from Ibn Sayyad before Ibn Sayyad could see him. The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) saw him lying on a bed, wrapped in a velvet cloak, murmuring. The mother of Ibn Sayyad saw the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) as he was concealing himself behind the palm trunks, and she said to Ibn Sayyad (that the Messenger of Allah had come). The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "If only you had left him (without alerting him)."'"

Ibn 'Umar said: "Then the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) stood up among the people, praised Allah as He deserves to be praised, and then mentioned the Dajjal. He said: 'I warn you of him. There has been no Prophet but that he warned his people of him. Nuh warned his people of him. But I will say to you concerning him something that no Prophet has said to his people: Know that he is one-eyed, and that Allah is not one-eyed.'"
15 : 87:
Narrated Abu Hurayrah: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "The Euphrates is about to uncover a treasure of gold, so whoever is present at that time should not take anything from it."

This was also narrated to us by Ahmad ibn Hamdan following this chain: Al-Ashajj narrated to us, Uqbah ibn Khalid narrated to us, who said: Ubaydullah ibn Umar narrated to us, who said: Abu Az-Zinad narrated to us, from Al-A'raj, from Abu Hurayrah, from the Prophet (ﷺ), similarly, except that he said: "It will uncover a mountain of gold."
16 : 104: Narrated 'Aisha: Does Abu Hurayrah not amaze you? He came and sat by the door of my chamber, narrating from the Prophet ﷺ, letting me hear that, while I was performing my prayer (tasbih). He got up before I finished my prayer, and had I caught up with him, I would have refuted him: Verily, the Messenger of Allah ﷺ did not narrate speech in rapid succession as you do.
16 : 278: Narrated Ibn 'Umar: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said concerning Ghifar: "May Allah forgive them," and concerning Aslam: "May Allah grant them safety," and concerning 'Usayyah: "They disobeyed Allah and His Messenger."
16 : 102:
Narrated Abu Hurayrah: A severe hunger afflicted me, so I met 'Umar bin Al-Khattab (may Allah be pleased with him) and asked him to recite a verse from the Book of Allah to me. He went into his house and recited it to me. I walked a short distance, then fell face down out of hunger. Suddenly, the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) was standing over my head, and he said: "O Abu Hurayrah!" I said: "Here I am, O Messenger of Allah, at your service." He took my hand and helped me up, and he recognized what was wrong with me. He went to his dwelling and ordered a large bowl of milk for me, and I drank from it. Then he said: "Have more, O Abu Hurayrah." So I drank again, until my stomach became full and round like a bow.

He (Abu Hurayrah) said: Then I saw 'Umar and mentioned to him what had happened to me, and I said to him: "Who had more right to this than you, O 'Umar? By Allah, I asked you to recite the verse to me, yet I am more capable of reciting it than you." 'Umar said: "By Allah, that I should have brought you in is more beloved to me than possessing red camels."
16 : 268: Narrated Ibn Shafi', who was a physician: Usayd ibn Hudayr summoned me, and I cauterized [treated] his sciatic vein, and he related to me two narrations. He said: The people of two households from my people came to me - the family of a household from Banu Zafar, and the family of a household from Banu Mu'awiyah - and they said: "Speak to the Prophet ﷺ so that he may allot a share for us, or give us [something]." So I spoke to the Prophet ﷺ, and he said: "Yes, I shall allot to the people of each household among them a portion, and if Allah grants us more, we shall grant them more." I said: "May Allah reward you with good, O Messenger of Allah." He said: "And you as well, may Allah reward you with good, for indeed I have not known you but to be chaste and patient."
16 : 417: Narrated Abu Sa'eed al-Khudri: The Prophet (ﷺ) said: "When a believer in Paradise desires a child, its conception, birth, and growth to maturity occur in a single hour, just as he wishes."
16 : 418: Narrated Abu Sa'id al-Khudri: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "...and raised couches. By the One in Whose Hand is my soul, their height is like the distance between the heaven and the earth, and indeed the distance between the heaven and the earth is a journey of five hundred years."
16 : 276: Qudamah bin Ibrahim said: "I saw Al-Hajjaj beating Abbas bin Sahl during the governorship of Ibn Al-Zubayr. So Sahl bin Sa'd came to him, and he was an old man with two braids, wearing two garments - a waist-wrap and a cloak - and he stood between the two rows and said: 'O Hajjaj, do you not remember the instruction of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) concerning us?' He said: 'What did the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) instruct concerning you?' He said: 'He instructed that good treatment be given to the good-doers among the Ansar, and that their wrongdoers be forgiven.'"
16 : 279: Shu'bah said: The chief of Banu Tamim, Muhammad ibn 'Abdullah ibn Abi Ya'qub Ad-Dabbi, narrated to me, from 'Abdur-Rahman ibn Abi Bakrah, from his father, who said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "What do you think? If Aslam, Ghifar, Juhaynah, and Muzaynah were better than Banu Tamim, Banu 'Amir ibn Sa'sa'ah, Asad, and Ghatafan, would those latter tribes have failed and lost out?" They said: "Yes." He said: "By the One in Whose Hand is my soul, indeed they (the former) are better than them (the latter)."
22: Narrated Abu Hurayrah: I heard the Messenger of Allah ﷺ say: "Allah said: 'The son of Adam abuses [reviles] Ad-Dahr (Time), while I am Ad-Dahr; in My Hand are the night and the day.'"
16 : 98: Narrated Khuzaymah ibn Thabit ibn Khuzaymah ibn Thabit - the one whose testimony the Prophet ﷺ made equivalent to the testimony of two men: Khuzaymah ibn Thabit saw in a dream that he prostrated upon the forehead of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ. So Khuzaymah came to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ and told him about it. He said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ then lay down for him, and said: "Fulfill your dream." So he prostrated upon the forehead of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ.
23: Narrated Abu Hurairah: The Prophet (ﷺ) said: "Allah, Mighty and Sublime, says: 'The son of Adam wrongs Me, for he abuses Ad-Dahr (Time), while I am Ad-Dahr. In My Hand is the command, and I alternate the night and the day, and when I wish, I take hold of them both.'"
30: Narrated Abu Hurayrah: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "I saw in a dream that I had two gold bracelets on my hands, so I blew on them and they flew away. I interpreted them as the two liars: Musaylimah and Al-'Ansi."
31: Narrated Abu Hurayrah: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "While I was sleeping, I saw in a dream as if there were two golden bracelets on my hands, and this troubled me greatly. Then it was revealed to me that I should blow on them, so I blew on them, and they flew away. I interpreted them as the two liars who would appear after me: Al-'Ansi, the man of Sana'a, and Musaylimah, the man of Al-Yamamah."
29: Narrated Abu Bakrah: The people spoke a great deal about the affair of Musaylimah the Liar before the Prophet ﷺ had said anything about him. Then the Messenger of Allah ﷺ stood up among the people, praised Allah as He deserves to be praised, and then said: "To proceed: As for the affair of this man about whom you have spoken so much, he is one liar among thirty liars who will appear before the Dajjal. There is no land but that the terror of the Messiah (Dajjal) will enter it, except Madinah; at every one of its mountain passes there are two angels warding off from it the terror of the Messiah."
37: Narrated 'Abdullah: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "When Allah speaks with the revelation, the people of heaven hear a rattling sound like the dragging of a chain upon a rock, and they fall down unconscious. They remain in that state until Jibril comes to them, and when he comes to them, the fear is removed from their hearts. So they say: 'O Jibril, what did your Lord say?' He says: 'The truth.' So they call out: 'The truth, the truth.'"
38: Narrated 'Aishah: Al-Harith bin Hisham asked the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), "O Messenger of Allah, how does the revelation come to you?" The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said, "Sometimes it comes to me like the ringing of a bell, and that is the hardest on me, then it leaves me after I have grasped what it said. And sometimes the angel takes the form of a man and speaks to me, and I grasp what he says." 'Aishah said: I indeed saw the revelation descending upon him on a severely cold, wintry day, and then it left him while his forehead was streaming with sweat.
35: Yahya bin Abi Kathir said: I asked Abu Salamah, "Which part of the Qur'an was revealed first?" He said, "O you wrapped in a cloak (Ya ayyuha al-Muddaththir)." I said, "Or was it Iqra (Recite)?" Abu Salamah said: I asked Jabir bin Abdullah about that, and he said, "O you wrapped in a cloak (Ya ayyuha al-Muddaththir)." I said, "Or was it Iqra?" He said: I will narrate to you what the Messenger of Allah ﷺ narrated to us. He said: "I secluded myself at Hira for a month. When I completed my seclusion, I came down and went into the depths of the valley. Suddenly I was called, so I looked in front of me, behind me, to my right, and to my left, but I did not see anyone. Then I was called again, so I looked up at the sky, and there he was [Jibril] on the Throne in the open air. A violent trembling seized me, so I went to Khadijah and said, 'Cover me,' so they covered me, then they poured water over me. Then Allah revealed to me: 'O you who is wrapped up (in garments)! Arise and warn! And your Lord magnify! And your garments purify!'"
36: Narrated Abu Hurayrah: that it reaches back to the Prophet ﷺ who said: "When Allah decrees a matter in the heaven, the angels beat their wings in submission to His saying, which resembles the sound of a chain being dragged on a rock, until fear is removed from their hearts. They say: 'What did your Lord say?' They say: 'He spoke the truth, and He is the All-Hearing, the All-Knowing.' Then the one who tries to steal a hearing listens to it, and sometimes the shooting star catches him before he can convey it to the one below him, and sometimes the shooting star does not catch him until he has conveyed it to the one below him." He said: "And they are like this, one below the other" - and Sufyan demonstrated this with his hand - "so this one passes it to that one, and that one to another, until it reaches the earth. It is then cast into the mouth of a soothsayer or a sorcerer, who mixes with it a hundred lies. Then he is believed, and it is said: 'Did he not say such and such on such and such a day, and it turned out to be true?' So he is believed because of that one true word which was heard from the heaven."
39: Narrated Ibn 'Abbas: Regarding the saying of Allah, "Do not move your tongue with it, to hasten with it" (Surah Al-Qiyamah, 75:16), he said: The Prophet (ﷺ) used to experience difficulty with the revelation, and he would move his lips. Ibn 'Abbas said: I move my lips just as the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) used to move them. Then Allah revealed: "Do not move your tongue with it to hasten with it. Indeed, upon Us is its collection and its recitation." He said: Its collection is in your breast, then you recite it. "So when We have recited it, then follow its recitation" (75:18) - he said: So listen to it and be silent. "Then upon Us is its explanation" - then it is upon Us that you should recite it. He said: So when Gabriel would come to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), he would listen attentively, and when Gabriel departed, the Prophet (ﷺ) would recite it just as he had been made to recite it.
40: Narrated Al-Bara': When the verse "Not equal are those believers who sit at home..." was revealed, the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Call Zaid for me, and let him bring the tablet and the inkwell," or "the shoulder-bone and the inkwell." Then he said: "Write: 'Not equal are those believers who sit at home and those who strive in the cause of Allah.'" He (Al-Bara') said: Behind the back of the Prophet (ﷺ) was 'Amr ibn Umm Maktum, the blind man, who said: "O Messenger of Allah, what do you command me to do, for I am a man of impaired sight?" Al-Bara' said: So there was revealed in its place: "except those who are disabled (by injury or are blind or lame)."
34:
Yahya bin Abi Kathir said: I asked Abu Salamah, "Which part of the Qur'an was revealed first?" He said, "Ya ayyuha al-Muddaththir (O you wrapped up in garments)." I said, "I have been informed that the first surah revealed of the Qur'an was Iqra' bismi Rabbika-l-ladhi khalaq (Recite in the name of your Lord who created)." Abu Salamah said: I asked Jabir bin Abdullah, "Which part of the Qur'an was revealed first?" He said, "Ya ayyuha al-Muddaththir." I said to him, "I have been informed that the first surah revealed of the Qur'an was Iqra' bismi Rabbika (Recite in the name of your Lord)." Jabir said: I will only narrate to you what the Messenger of Allah ﷺ narrated to us. He said: "I secluded myself at Hira, and when I completed my seclusion, I came down and went into the depths of the valley. Then I was called, so I looked in front of me, behind me, to my right, and to my left, but I did not see anything. Then I was called again, so I looked above me, and there he was, sitting on a throne between the heaven and the earth. I was terrified by him, so I went to Khadijah and said, 'Wrap me up, wrap me up,' and they poured cold water on me. Then it was revealed to me: 'O you who is wrapped up [in garments]! Arise and warn, and magnify your Lord.'"

Abu Hatim said: In this report of Jabir, it states that the first thing revealed of the Qur'an was "Ya ayyuha al-Muddaththir" (Surat al-Muddaththir, verse 1), while in the report of A'ishah it is "Iqra' bismi Rabbika." There is no contradiction between these two reports, for Allah, Mighty and Sublime, revealed to His Messenger ﷺ "Iqra' bismi Rabbika" while he was in the cave at Hira. Then, when he returned to his house, Khadijah wrapped him up and poured cold water upon him, and it was revealed to him in Khadijah's house, "Ya ayyuha al-Muddaththir, qum" (O you who is wrapped up, arise), without there being any inconsistency or contradiction between the two reports.
41: Narrated Al-Bara' ibn 'Azib: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said, "Bring me the shoulder-blade or the tablet." So he wrote: "Not equal are those believers who sit [at home]," while 'Amr ibn Umm Maktum was behind him. He said, "Is there any dispensation for me?" So there was revealed: "except those who are disabled (by injury or are blind or lame)."
42: Narrated Al-Bara': When this verse was revealed: "Not equal are those believers who sit [at home]," the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) called for Zaid, who came with a shoulder blade (to write on), and he wrote it upon it. Then Ibn Umm Maktum complained of his blindness, so the verse "other than those who are disabled (by injury or disease)" was revealed.
33:
Narrated 'Aishah: The first thing with which the revelation began for the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) was true dreams in his sleep. He would never see a dream but it would come true like the break of dawn. Then solitude was made dear to him, and he used to go to the cave of Hira' and worship there - that is, devote himself to worship - for a number of nights before returning to his family. He would take provisions for that purpose, then return to Khadijah and take provisions again for a similar period, until the Truth came to him suddenly while he was in the cave of Hira'. The angel came to him and said: "Recite!" The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "I said: 'I am not one who recites.' He then took hold of me and pressed me until I reached the limit of my endurance. Then he released me and said: 'Recite!' I said: 'I am not one who recites.' He took hold of me and pressed me a second time until I reached the limit of my endurance. Then he released me and said: 'Recite!' I said: 'I am not one who recites.' He took hold of me and pressed me a third time until I reached the limit of my endurance. Then he released me and said: 'Recite in the name of your Lord who created' - up to - 'that which he knew not.'"

He (the Prophet) returned with it, his shoulders trembling, until he entered upon Khadijah and said: "Cover me! Cover me!" So they covered him until his fear left him. Then he said: "O Khadijah, what is wrong with me?" And he told her what had happened, and said: "I fear that something may happen to me." She said: "Never! Rejoice, for by Allah, Allah will never disgrace you. You maintain the ties of kinship, you speak the truth, you bear the burdens of the weak, you provide hospitality to the guest, and you help in matters of truth and justice."

Then Khadijah took him to Waraqah ibn Nawfal, who was her cousin (the son of her father's brother). He had embraced Christianity during the pre-Islamic period of ignorance, and he used to write in Arabic script, writing from the Gospel in Arabic whatever he wished to write. He was an old man who had lost his sight. Khadijah said to him: "O my cousin, listen to what your nephew has to say." Waraqah said: "O my nephew, what have you seen?" So the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) told him what he had seen. Waraqah said: "This is the Namus (the same one who used to bring revelation) who was sent down to Musa. Would that I were young again so that I might be alive when your people drive you out!" The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Will they drive me out?" Waraqah said: "Yes. No man has ever come with something like what you have brought, but he was met with hostility. If I should live to see that day, I will support you strongly."

Not long after, Waraqah died, and the revelation ceased for a while, until the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), as we have been told, became so distressed that he went out several times intending to throw himself off the high mountain peaks. But every time he reached the summit of a mountain to throw himself down, Jibril would appear to him and say: "O Muhammad, you are indeed the Messenger of Allah in truth." This would calm his heart and settle his soul, and he would return. Then, when the interval of revelation grew long, he would go out again for the same purpose, and upon reaching the mountain peak, Jibril would appear to him again and say the same thing to him.
44: Narrated Al-Zuhri: A man came to him while I was listening and said, "O Abu Bakr, for how long was revelation withheld from the Prophet of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, before his death?" He said, "No one has asked me about this since I learned it from Anas ibn Malik." Anas ibn Malik said: "He was taken from this world when it (revelation) was more abundant than it had ever been."
46: Narrated Anas: The Prophet ﷺ was brought al-Buraq, saddled and bridled, on the night he was taken on the Night Journey, so that he might ride it, but it became stubborn. Jibril said to it: "What makes you do this? By Allah, no one has ever ridden you who is more honored by Allah than he is." He (Anas) said: So it broke out in sweat.
47: Narrated Buraydah: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "On the night I was taken on the Night Journey, I arrived at Bayt al-Maqdis (Jerusalem), and Jibra'il pierced the rock with his finger and tethered al-Buraq to it."
43: Narrated Ibn 'Abbas: I said to 'Uthman bin 'Affan, "What made you join Al-Anfal, which is one of the Mathani (short surahs), with Bara'ah (At-Tawbah), which is one of the Mi'in (long surahs), and place them together?" 'Uthman said, "Whenever a verse of the Qur'an was revealed, the Prophet (ﷺ) would summon one of those who wrote for him and say, 'Put this in the surah in which such and such is mentioned.' Al-Anfal was revealed in Madinah, and Bara'ah was revealed in Madinah near the end of the Qur'an, and its subject matter resembled that of Al-Anfal. So the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) passed away without informing us where to place it. I therefore concluded that its account was similar to that of Al-Anfal, so I joined the two together, and we did not write the line 'Bismillah ir-Rahman ir-Rahim' between them. I then placed it among the seven long surahs (As-Sab' At-Tiwal)."
49: Narrated Anas bin Malik: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "On the night I was taken on the Night Journey (Isra), I passed by Musa (peace be upon him) praying in his grave."
45: Narrated Zirr ibn Hubaysh: I came to Hudhayfah, and he said: "Who are you, O bald one?" I said: "I am Zirr ibn Hubaysh; tell me about the prayer of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) in Bayt al-Maqdis (Jerusalem) when he was taken on the Night Journey." He said: "Who informed you of this, O bald one?" I said: "The Qur'an." He said: "The Qur'an?" So I recited: "Glory be to Him Who took His servant for a journey by night" - and this was the recitation of 'Abdullah - up to His saying: "Indeed, He is the All-Hearing, the All-Seeing." He said: "Do you see that he prayed therein?" I said: "No." He said: "A mount was brought to him." Hammad said: 'Asim described it, but I do not remember its description. He said: Jibril mounted him upon it, one of them riding behind the other, and he set off with him that night until he came to Bayt al-Maqdis, and he was shown what is in the heavens and what is on the earth. Then the two of them returned as they had come, and he did not pray therein. Had he prayed, it would have been a Sunnah.
51: Narrated Abu Hurayrah: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "On the night I was taken on the Night Journey, I met Musa, a man with straight hair, as if he were one of the men of Shanu'ah. And I met 'Isa, a reddish man, as if he had just come out of a Diemas - meaning a bathhouse. And I saw Ibrahim, and I am the one who most resembles him among his descendants. Then I was brought two vessels: one containing wine, and the other containing milk. It was said to me: 'Take whichever of them you wish.' So I took the milk, and it was said to me: 'You have been guided to the Fitrah (natural disposition). Had you taken the wine, your nation would have gone astray.'"
52: Narrated Abu Hurairah: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ was brought two vessels on the night he was taken on the Night Journey (Isra), one containing wine and the other milk. He looked at them, then took the milk, and Jibril (peace be upon him) said to him: "You have been guided to the Fitrah (natural disposition); had you taken the wine, your nation would have gone astray."
53: Narrated Anas ibn Malik: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "On the night I was taken on the Night Journey, I saw men whose lips were being cut with scissors of fire. I said: 'Who are these, O Gabriel?' He said: 'They are the preachers from among your nation who command people to righteousness but forget themselves, while they recite the Book. Do they not understand?'"
55: Narrated Jabir bin 'Abdullah: I heard the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) say: "When the Quraysh disbelieved me, I stood up in Al-Hijr, and Allah displayed Jerusalem (Bait Al-Maqdis) before me, and I began to inform them of its signs while I was looking at it."
54: Narrated Anas ibn Malik: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "I entered Paradise, and I saw a palace made of gold. I said: 'To whom does this palace belong?' They said: 'To a young man from the Quraysh.' I thought it was mine, so I said: 'Who is he?' It was said: 'Umar ibn al-Khattab.' O Abu Hafs, were it not for the jealousy I know you possess, I would have entered it." He said: "O Messenger of Allah, would I be jealous of anyone but you? Indeed, I would never be jealous of you."
56: Narrated Ibn 'Abbas: Regarding the words of Allah, the Exalted: "And We did not make the vision which We showed you except as a trial for the people," he said: "It was a vision of the eye which the Messenger of Allah, may Allah's peace and blessings be upon him, was shown on the night he was taken on the Night Journey."
57:
Narrated Ibn 'Abbas: Muhammad (ﷺ) did indeed see his Lord.

Abu Hatim said: The meaning of the statement of Ibn 'Abbas, "Muhammad (ﷺ) did indeed see his Lord," is that he intended by it that he saw Him with his heart, in that station of honor and elevation which no human being has ever ascended to.
58:
Narrated Abdullah bin Shaqiq Al-'Uqayli: I said to Abu Dharr, "If I had seen the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, I would have asked him about everything." He said, "What would you have asked him about?" I said, "I would have asked him: Did you see your Lord?" He said, "I did ask him that, and he said: 'I saw a light.'"

Abu Hatim said: Its meaning is that he did not see his Lord, but rather he saw a light from among the created lights, a light from above.
61: Narrated Qurrah: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "A group of my nation will continue to be victorious, and those who forsake them will not harm them, until the Hour comes."
62: Narrated Ibn 'Abbas: The Prophet ﷺ said: "You will hear (Hadith), and it will be heard from you, and it will be heard from those who heard it from you."
59:
Narrated Ibn Mas'ud: Regarding the saying of Allah, the Exalted, "The heart did not lie about what it saw" (53:11), he said: "The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) saw Gabriel in a garment of ruby, which had filled what is between the heaven and the earth."

Abu Hatim said: Allah, the Exalted, had commanded Gabriel on the Night of the Journey to teach Muhammad (ﷺ) what he needed to know, just as He said: "Taught by one intense in strength, possessed of soundness; and he settled" (53:5-6), meaning by this Gabriel; "Then he approached and descended" (53:8), meaning by this Gabriel; "so he was at a distance of two bow-lengths or nearer" (53:9), meaning by this Gabriel; "And He revealed to His servant what He revealed" (53:10) through Gabriel; "The heart did not lie about what it saw" (53:11), meaning that he saw his Lord with his heart in that noble station, and he saw Gabriel in a garment of ruby, which had filled what is between the heaven and the earth, in accordance with what is stated in the report from Ibn Mas'ud which we have mentioned.
65:
Narrated Abu Dharr: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ left us (with such comprehensive teachings) that there is not even a bird that flaps its wings in the sky but we have some knowledge of it from him.

Abu Hatim said: The meaning of "we have some knowledge of it from him" refers to his ﷺ commands, prohibitions, reports, actions, and permissions.
66: Narrated Abdullah ibn Mas'ud: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "May Allah make radiant a man who hears a hadith from us and conveys it just as he heard it, for many a one to whom it is conveyed retains it better than the one who heard it."
63: Narrated Abu Humayd and Abu Usayd: The Prophet ﷺ said: "When you hear a narration from me which your hearts recognize, and your hair and skin become soft (tranquil) for it, and you see that it is close to you, then I am the closest of you to it. And when you hear a narration from me which your hearts deny, and your hair and skin recoil from it, and you see that it is far removed from you, then I am the furthest of you from it."
64:
Narrated Abu Sa'eed al-Khudri: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Do not write anything from me except the Qur'an. Whoever has written anything from me other than that, let him erase it."

Abu Hatim (may Allah be pleased with him) said: His (ﷺ) prohibition of writing anything from him besides the Qur'an was intended to encourage the memorization of the Sunan, rather than relying on writing them down while neglecting their memorization and the understanding of them. The proof of the soundness of this is that he (ﷺ) permitted Abu Shah to write down the sermon which he had heard from the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), and he (ﷺ) gave permission to 'Abdullah ibn 'Amr to write.
68: Narrated Ibn Mas'ud: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "May Allah have mercy on a person who hears a Hadith from me and conveys it just as he heard it, for perhaps the one to whom it is conveyed will be more retentive of it than the one who heard it."
69: Narrated 'Abdullah ibn Mas'ud: I heard the Prophet ﷺ say: "May Allah brighten the face of a man who hears a saying from us and conveys it just as he heard it, for many a person to whom something is conveyed retains it better than the one who heard it directly."
60:
Narrated Masruq bin al-Ajda': that he heard 'Aishah say: "The greatest lie against Allah is that of one who says that Muhammad (ﷺ) saw his Lord, or that Muhammad (ﷺ) concealed something of the revelation, or that Muhammad (ﷺ) knew what tomorrow holds." It was said to her: "O Mother of the Believers, then what did he see?" She said: "No, that was only Gabriel; he saw him twice in his true form: once when he filled the horizon, and once when he blocked the horizon of the sky."

Abu Hatim said: One who is not skilled in the science of Hadith may imagine that these two reports contradict each other, but they do not. For Allah, Mighty and Exalted, favored His Messenger (ﷺ) above the rest of the Prophets, to the extent that Gabriel came nearer to his Lord than the span of two bow-lengths, and Muhammad (ﷺ) was being taught by Gabriel at that time. So he (ﷺ) saw Him with his heart, as He willed. As for the report of 'Aishah and its interpretation, she meant that he did not perceive Him—whether in sleep or in wakefulness. As for His saying: "No vision can grasp Him," its meaning is that no vision can grasp Him, [though] He will be seen on the Day of Resurrection, yet no vision that sees Him will grasp Him fully, for "grasping" (idrak) means encompassing, while "seeing" (ru'yah) means looking. Allah is seen, but His true essence is not grasped, for grasping applies to created beings, while looking is what occurs from the servant toward his Lord. The report of 'Aishah that no vision can grasp Him means that no vision can grasp Him in this world or in the Hereafter, except for one whom He favors among His servants by making him fit for that. The term "this world" (al-dunya) may apply to the earths and the heavens and what is between them, for these things are beginnings which Allah, Mighty and Exalted, created so that deeds of obedience might be earned in them for the Hereafter, which comes after this beginning. So the Prophet (ﷺ) saw his Lord in a place to which the name "this world" does not apply, for he was, at that time, nearer to Him than the span of two bow-lengths—so that the report of 'Aishah means that he (ﷺ) did not see Him in this world, without there being any contradiction or discrepancy between the two reports.
70: Narrated Ibn 'Umar: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "The keys of the unseen are five: No one knows what the wombs will bring forth except Allah; no one knows what will happen tomorrow except Allah; no one knows when the rain will come except Allah; no soul knows in what land it will die; and no one knows when the Hour will come except Allah."
71: Narrated Ibn 'Umar: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "The keys of the unseen are five which none knows except Allah: none knows what the wombs conceal except Allah, none knows what is in tomorrow except Allah, none knows when the rain will come except Allah, no soul knows in what land it will die, and none knows when the Hour will come except Allah."
67:
Narrated Abu Abdur Rahman bin Aban (Ibn Uthman bin Affan), on the authority of his father: Zaid bin Thabit came out from Marwan's presence close to midday, so I said: He would not have sent for him except concerning something he wanted to ask him about. So I got up and went to him and asked him, and he said: Indeed, he asked us about things we had heard from the Messenger of Allah ﷺ:

"May Allah have mercy on a man who hears a Hadith from me and memorizes it, so that he conveys it to others, for many a bearer of knowledge conveys it to one who is more learned than himself, and many a bearer of knowledge is not himself learned. There are three qualities upon which the heart of a Muslim will not harbor deceit: sincerity of action for the sake of Allah, sincere counsel to those in authority, and adherence to the Muslim community, for their call surrounds them from behind."
72: Narrated Abu Hurayrah: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Indeed, Allah hates every harsh and coarse person who is a loudmouth in the marketplaces, a corpse by night, a donkey by day, knowledgeable about the affairs of this world but ignorant of the affairs of the Hereafter."
75: Narrated Ibn Mas'ud: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "The Qur'an was revealed in seven modes (Ahruf); for every verse of it there is an outward meaning (Zahr) and an inward meaning (Batn)."
73: Narrated Aisha: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) recited the words of Allah, "It is He who has sent down to you the Book; in it are verses [that are] precise..." to the end of it, and said: "If you see those who follow that which is unclear (ambiguous) in it, then know that they are the ones whom Allah has meant, so beware of them."
77: Narrated Jabir: The Messenger of Allah said: "Do not seek knowledge in order to boast about it to the scholars, nor to argue with it against the foolish, nor to show off with it in gatherings. Whoever does that, then the Fire, the Fire."
74:
Narrated Abu Hurayrah: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "The Qur'an was revealed according to seven modes of recitation (Ahruf), and disputation concerning the Qur'an is disbelief" - he said this three times - "so whatever of it you know, act upon it, and whatever of it you do not know, refer it to one who knows it."

Abu Hatim, may Allah be pleased with him, said: His saying (ﷺ), "whatever of it you know, act upon it" implies within it the notion of capability, meaning: act upon what you know of the Book to the extent that you are able. And his saying, "whatever of it you do not know, refer it to one who knows it" contains a warning against the opposite of this command, namely that they should not ask one who does not know.
76:
Narrated 'Aishah: The Prophet of Allah (ﷺ) recited this verse: "It is He Who has sent down to you the Book; in it are verses that are entirely clear and precise, they are the foundation of the Book, and others not entirely clear" (Surah Aal 'Imran 3:7) up to His saying "those of understanding" (Surah Al-Baqarah 2:269).

She said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) then said: "Have you seen those who dispute concerning it? They are the ones whom Allah meant, so beware of them."

Matar said: I remember that he said: "Do not sit with them, for they are the ones whom Allah meant, so beware of them."

Abu Hatim said: Ayyub heard this report from both Matar Al-Warraq and Ibn Abi Mulaykah.
48:
Narrated Malik ibn Sa'sa'ah: The Prophet of Allah (ﷺ) narrated to them about the night he was taken on the Night Journey. He said: "While I was in Al-Hatim" - and sometimes he said, "in Al-Hijr" - "a visitor came to me and cut open [my chest] from here to here." I said to Al-Jarud, who was beside me: "What does he mean by that?" He said: "From the top of his chest to below his navel." "He then took out my heart, and I was brought a golden basin filled with faith and wisdom, and my heart was washed and then filled [with faith and wisdom]. Then I was brought a white animal, smaller than a mule and larger than a donkey." Al-Jarud said to him: "Was it Al-Buraq, O Abu Hamzah?" Anas said: "Yes, its stride would reach as far as its eye could see. So I was mounted upon it, and Jibril set off with me until he reached the lowest heaven. He asked for it to be opened, and it was said: 'Who is this?' He said: 'Jibril.' It was said: 'Who is with you?' He said: 'Muhammad (ﷺ).' It was said: 'Has he been sent for?' He said: 'Yes.' It was said: 'Welcome to him, what an excellent visit he has made!' So it was opened, and when I entered, there was Adam. He said: 'This is your father Adam, so greet him.' I greeted him, and he returned the greeting, then said: 'Welcome, righteous son and righteous Prophet!'

"Then he ascended with me until he reached the second heaven and asked for it to be opened. It was said: 'Who is this?' He said: 'Jibril.' It was said: 'Who is with you?' He said: 'Muhammad.' It was said: 'Has he been sent for?' He said: 'Yes.' It was said: 'Welcome to him, what an excellent visit he has made!' So it was opened, and when I entered, there were Yahya and 'Isa, who are cousins. He said: 'These are Yahya and 'Isa, so greet them.' I greeted them, and they returned the greeting, then said: 'Welcome, righteous brother and righteous Prophet!'

"Then he ascended with me to the third heaven and asked for it to be opened. It was said: 'Who is this?' He said: 'Jibril.' It was said: 'Who is with you?' He said: 'Muhammad (ﷺ).' It was said: 'Has he been sent for?' He said: 'Yes.' It was said: 'Welcome to him, what an excellent visit he has made!' So it was opened, and when I entered, there was Yusuf. He said: 'This is Yusuf, so greet him.' I greeted him, and he returned the greeting, then said: 'Welcome, righteous brother and righteous Prophet!'

"Then he ascended with me until he reached the fourth heaven and asked for it to be opened. It was said: 'Who is this?' He said: 'Jibril.' It was said: 'Who is with you?' He said: 'Muhammad (ﷺ).' It was said: 'Has he indeed been sent for?' He said: 'Yes.' It was said: 'Welcome to him, what an excellent visit he has made!' So it was opened, and when I entered, there was Idris. He said: 'This is Idris, so greet him.' I greeted him, and he returned the greeting, then said: 'Welcome, righteous brother and righteous Prophet!'

"Then he ascended with me until he reached the fifth heaven and asked for it to be opened. It was said: 'Who is this?' He said: 'Jibril.' It was said: 'Who is with you?' He said: 'Muhammad (ﷺ).' It was said: 'Has he been sent for?' He said: 'Yes.' It was said: 'Welcome to him, what an excellent visit he has made!' So it was opened, and when I entered, there was Harun. He said: 'This is Harun, so greet him.' I greeted him, and he returned the greeting, then said: 'Welcome, righteous brother and righteous Prophet!'

"Then he ascended with me until he reached the sixth heaven and asked for it to be opened. It was said: 'Who is this?' He said: 'Jibril.' It was said: 'Who is with you?' He said: 'Muhammad (ﷺ).' It was said: 'Has he indeed been sent for?' He said: 'Yes.' It was said: 'Welcome to him, what an excellent visit he has made!' So it was opened, and when I entered, there was Musa. He said: 'This is Musa, so greet him.' I greeted him, and he returned the greeting, then said: 'Welcome, righteous brother and righteous Prophet!' When I passed by him, he wept. He was asked: 'What makes you weep?' He said: 'I weep because a young man has been sent after me whose followers who will enter Paradise are more numerous than those of my followers who will enter it.'

"Then he ascended with me until he reached the seventh heaven and asked for it to be opened. It was said: 'Who is this?' He said: 'Jibril.' It was said: 'Who is with you?' He said: 'Muhammad (ﷺ).' It was said: 'Has he been sent for?' He said: 'Yes.' It was said: 'Welcome to him, what an excellent visit he has made!' So it was opened, and when I entered, there was Ibrahim. He said: 'This is your father Ibrahim, so greet him.' I greeted him, and he returned the greeting, then said: 'Welcome, righteous son and righteous Prophet!'

"Then I was raised up to Sidrat al-Muntaha, and its fruit was like the jars of Hajar, and its leaves were like the ears of elephants. He said: 'This is Sidrat al-Muntaha.' And there were four rivers, two hidden and two visible. I said: 'What are these, O Jibril?' He said: 'As for the two hidden ones, they are two rivers in Paradise; and as for the two visible ones, they are the Nile and the Euphrates.' Then Al-Bayt al-Ma'mur was raised up for me."

Qatadah said: Al-Hasan also narrated to us from Abu Hurayrah, from the Prophet (ﷺ), that he saw Al-Bayt al-Ma'mur, and that seventy thousand angels enter it every day, then never return to it.

Then he returned to the narration of Anas: "Then I was brought vessels of wine, milk, and honey, and I took the milk. He said: 'This is the natural inclination (Al-Fitrah) upon which you and your nation stand.'

"Then the prayer was made obligatory upon me: fifty prayers every day. So I went back and passed by Musa, and he said: 'What have you been commanded?' I said: 'I have been commanded with fifty prayers every day.' He said: 'Your nation will not be able to bear fifty prayers every day, and I have tried the people before you, and I struggled most severely with the Children of Israel. So go back to your Lord and ask Him to lighten the burden for your nation.' So I went back, and He removed ten from me. I returned to Musa, and he said the same. I went back, and He removed ten more from me. I returned to Musa, and he said the same. I went back, and He removed ten more from me. I returned to Musa, and he said the same. I went back, and I was commanded with ten prayers every day. I returned to Musa, and he said the same. I went back, and I was commanded with five prayers every day. I returned to Musa, and he said: 'What have you been commanded?' I said: 'I have been commanded with five prayers every day.' He said: 'Your nation will not be able to bear five prayers every day, and I have tried the people before you, and I struggled most severely with the Children of Israel. So go back to your Lord and ask Him to lighten the burden for your nation.'" He said: "I said: 'I have asked my Lord until I feel ashamed, but I am content and I submit.' Then when I passed on, a caller called out: 'I have carried out My obligation and have lightened the burden for My servants.'"
78: Narrated Abu Hurayrah: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Whoever learns knowledge which is sought for the sake of Allah, but he only learns it to gain some worldly benefit through it, will not find the fragrance of Paradise on the Day of Resurrection."
80: Narrated Imran ibn Husain: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "The thing I fear most for you is the disputation of the hypocrite who is eloquent of tongue."
79: Narrated 'Umar ibn al-Khattab: I heard the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) saying: "Do not sit with the people of Qadr (those who deny predestination), and do not initiate discussion with them."
82: Narrated Jabir bin 'Abdullah: I heard the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) saying: "O Allah, I ask You for beneficial knowledge, and I seek refuge with You from knowledge that does not benefit."
84: Narrated Abu Hurayrah: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Whoever takes a path seeking knowledge therein, Allah will make easy for him a path to Paradise thereby. And whoever is slowed down by his deeds, his lineage will not hasten him."
83: Narrated Anas ibn Malik: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) used to say: "O Allah, I seek refuge in You from knowledge that does not benefit, a deed that is not raised up, a heart that does not fear, and a supplication that is not heard."
81: Narrated Hudhayfah: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "I only fear for you a man who read the Qur'an until its splendor was seen upon him, and he was a support for Islam, but then he changed [it] to whatever Allah willed, so he cast it off, threw it behind his back, and attacked his neighbor with the sword, accusing him of shirk." I [Jundab] said: "O Prophet of Allah, which of them is more deserving of shirk, the one accused or the one who accused him?" He said: "Rather, the one who accused him."
85: Narrated Zirr: I came to Safwan ibn 'Assal al-Muradi, and he said: "What has brought you here?" I said: "I have come to seek out knowledge." He said: "I heard the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) say: 'There is no one who goes out of his house seeking knowledge, but the angels lower their wings for him, pleased with what he does.'"
87: Narrated Abu Hurayrah: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "Whoever enters this mosque of ours to learn something good or to teach it, is like one who strives in the cause of Allah. And whoever enters it for any other purpose is like one who looks at what does not belong to him."
86: Narrated Abu Waqid al-Laythi: While the Messenger of Allah ﷺ was sitting in the mosque with the people around him, three men approached. Two of them came toward the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, while one went away. When the two stopped before the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, they greeted him with salam. One of them saw an opening in the circle and sat in it, while the other sat behind them. As for the third, he turned away and left. When the Messenger of Allah ﷺ finished, he said: "Shall I not inform you about the three men? As for one of them, he sought shelter in Allah, so Allah sheltered him. As for the other, Allah felt shy before him (and had mercy on him). But as for the last, he turned away, so Allah turned away from him."
50:
Anas ibn Malik narrated: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said, "I passed by Musa on the night I was taken on the Night Journey, and he was standing, performing prayer in his grave, near the red sand-hill."

Abu Hatim said: Allah, Mighty and Exalted, has power over whatever He wills. He may promise something for an appointed time, then decree that some portion of that thing occur before the arrival of that time—just as He promised the resurrection of the dead on the Day of Judgment and set it as a fixed appointed time, yet He decreed the occurrence of something similar to it in certain instances, such as the one whom Allah mentioned and related in His Book, where He says: "Or [consider] the one who passed by a township which had fallen into ruin. He said, 'How will Allah bring this to life after its death?' So Allah caused him to die for a hundred years; then He revived him. He said, 'How long have you remained?' He said, 'I have remained a day or part of a day.' He said, 'Rather, you have remained for a hundred years...'" to the end of the verse—and like Allah's, Mighty and Exalted, reviving of the dead through the hands of 'Isa ibn Maryam, upon him be Allah's blessings. Since the occurrence of this state among mankind before the Day of Judgment was established as something Allah, Mighty and Exalted, willed, it is not to be denied that Allah, Mighty and Exalted, brought Musa to life in his grave, such that the Chosen One (ﷺ) passed by him on the night he was taken on the Night Journey.

This is because the grave of Musa is at Mudyan, between Madinah and Bayt al-Maqdis. So the Prophet (ﷺ) saw him supplicating in his grave, for prayer is supplication. Then, when the Prophet (ﷺ) entered Bayt al-Maqdis and was taken up [to the heavens], Musa too was taken up, until the Prophet saw him in the sixth heaven, and the conversation that took place between them is as we have already mentioned. Likewise is his seeing of the rest of the Prophets, as mentioned in the report of Malik ibn Sa'sa'ah.

As for the Prophet's (ﷺ) statement in the report of Malik ibn Sa'sa'ah: "While I was in al-Hatim, someone came to me and split open [my chest] from here to here"—this was a distinction granted to him above others, and it was one of the miracles of prophethood, for if the chest of an ordinary human being were split open at the location of the heart and his heart removed, he would die. His statement, "then it was filled," means that Allah, Mighty and Exalted, filled his heart with certainty and knowledge, which had been placed in the golden basin, and it was then transferred into his heart.

Then a mount called al-Buraq was brought to him, and he was carried upon it from al-Hatim or al-Hijr—both being within the Sacred Mosque. Jibril took him until he brought him to the grave of Musa, as we have described. Then he entered the mosque of Bayt al-Maqdis, and Jibril pierced the Rock with his finger and tethered al-Buraq to it, then ascended with him to the heavens. The mention of the tethering of al-Buraq to the Rock is found in the report of Buraydah, and the seeing of Musa (ﷺ) praying in his grave is not mentioned together with it in the report of Malik ibn Sa'sa'ah.

When he ascended with him to the lowest heaven, Jibril sought that it be opened. It was said: "Who is this?" He said: "Jibril." It was said: "And who is with you?" He said: "Muhammad (ﷺ)." It was said: "Has he been sent for?"—meaning: has he been sent for so that he may be taken up to the heavens—not that they were unaware of his mission up to that time, for the Night Journey occurred seven years after the descent of revelation began. When it was opened for him, he saw Adam, as we have described previously. Likewise he saw, in the second heaven, Yahya ibn Zakariyya and 'Isa ibn Maryam; in the third heaven, Yusuf ibn Ya'qub; in the fourth heaven, Idris; then in the fifth heaven, Harun; then in the sixth heaven, Musa; then in the seventh heaven, Ibrahim—for it is permissible that Allah, Mighty and Exalted, brought them to life so that the Chosen One (ﷺ) might see them on that night, this being a miraculous sign by which his prophethood is evidenced, in accordance with what we have established previously.

Then the Lote Tree of the Utmost Boundary was raised up for him, and he saw it in the state that he described. Then fifty prayers were made obligatory upon him. This was a matter of trial, by which Allah, Mighty and Exalted, willed to test His chosen one Muhammad (ﷺ), when He made fifty prayers obligatory upon him, even though it was already in Allah's foreknowledge that He would only make five prayers obligatory upon his nation. So He commanded him with fifty prayers as a matter of trial. This is like when we say: Allah, Mighty and Exalted, may command a matter, intending that the one commanded proceed toward carrying out His command, without intending that the thing itself actually come into existence—just as Allah, Mighty and Exalted, commanded His close friend Ibrahim to slaughter his son. He commanded him with this matter, intending thereby that he proceed to carry out His command, without the actual occurrence of the deed itself. So when the two of them submitted, and Ibrahim laid his son down upon his forehead, Allah ransomed him with a great sacrifice, for had Allah, Mighty and Exalted, willed the actual occurrence of what He commanded, he would have found his son slaughtered.

Likewise, He made prayer obligatory as fifty, intending thereby that the Prophet proceed to carry out His command, without the actual occurrence of the deed itself. So when he returned to Musa and informed him that he had been commanded with fifty prayers each day, Allah inspired Musa to tell Muhammad (ﷺ) to ask his Lord for a reduction for the sake of his nation. Allah, Mighty and Exalted, made Musa's words to him a means of manifesting the reality confirming what we have said: that the obligation which Allah intended to impose upon His servants was to come to five, not fifty. So the Prophet returned to Allah, Mighty and Exalted, and asked Him, and He removed ten from it. This too was a matter of trial, intended for its progression toward fulfillment without the actual occurrence of the deed itself. Then Allah made Musa's question to him a means for the execution of Allah's, Mighty and Exalted, decree in His prior knowledge, that prayer would be made obligatory upon this nation as five, not fifty, until the reduction reached five prayers. Then Allah, Mighty and Exalted, inspired His chosen one (ﷺ) at that point to say to Musa: "I have asked my Lord until I felt ashamed, but I am satisfied and I submit." When he passed by, a caller called out: "I have carried out My obligation"—meaning the five prayers—"and I have lightened the burden upon My servants"—meaning, relieved from His servants the matter of trial with which He had commanded them, namely the fifty prayers which we have mentioned.

All of these matters during the Night Journey were seen by the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) with his own body, in plain sight, and were not a vision or an image merely depicted for him. For if the Night Journey and what he saw during it had been a dream rather than actual wakeful experience, this would be inconceivable, since ordinary human beings may see in their sleep the heavens, the angels, the Prophets, Paradise, the Fire, and similar things. If the Chosen One's (ﷺ) seeing of what he described on the Night Journey had been in sleep rather than in wakefulness, this would have been a state in which ordinary human beings would be equal to him, since they see the like of it in their dreams, and his distinction would then be nullified, and it would not have been a miraculous state by which he was distinguished above others—contrary to the claim of those who reject these reports and deny Allah's, Mighty and Exalted, power and the execution of His judgment as He loves, in the manner He loves. Exalted and Sublime is our Lord above such a claim and its like.
89: Narrated Mu'awiyah bin Abi Sufyan: I heard the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) say: "Whoever Allah wishes good for, He grants him understanding of the religion."
90: Narrated Ibn Mas'ud: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "There is no envy except in two cases: a man to whom Allah has given wealth, and he uses it to spend it in the cause of truth; and a man to whom Allah has given wisdom, and he judges by it and teaches it."
91: Narrated Abu Hurayrah: I heard Abu al-Qasim (peace be upon him) say: "The best of you are those with the best character, so understand this well."
95: Narrated Abu Hurayrah: The Prophet ﷺ said: "Whoever conceals knowledge will be bridled with a bridle of fire on the Day of Resurrection."
94: Narrated 'Aishah: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Excuse the people of good character their faults."
93:
Narrated Abu Qatadah: I heard the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) say: "The best of what a man leaves behind him are three things: a righteous child who prays for him, ongoing charity whose reward reaches him, and knowledge that is benefited from after him."

Abu Hatim, may Allah be pleased with him, said: More than one hundred hadiths of this type remain, which we have distributed throughout the other sections of this book, because those places were more fitting for them.
92: Narrated Abu Hurayrah: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "People are like minerals in goodness and evil. The best of them in the Age of Ignorance (Jahiliyyah) are the best of them in Islam, when they [gain] understanding."
88:
Narrated Kathir ibn Qays: I was sitting with Abu al-Darda in the mosque of Damascus when a man came to him and said, "O Abu al-Darda, I have come to you from the city of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) concerning a hadith which has reached me that you narrate it from the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ)." Abu al-Darda said, "Have you not come for some need? Have you not come for trade? Have you come for nothing but this hadith?" He said, "Yes." Abu al-Darda said: I heard the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) say: "Whoever takes a path in search of knowledge, Allah will make easy for him a path to Paradise. The angels lower their wings in approval of the seeker of knowledge, and the scholar is prayed for forgiveness by everyone in the heavens and everyone on the earth, even the fish in the water. The superiority of the scholar over the worshipper is like the superiority of the moon on the night it is full over the rest of the stars. Indeed, the scholars are the heirs of the prophets, and the prophets did not leave behind gold or silver, but rather they left behind knowledge, and whoever takes it has taken an abundant share."

Abu Hatim, may Allah be pleased with him, said: In this hadith there is a clear explanation that the scholars who possess the merit we have mentioned are those who teach the knowledge of the Prophet (ﷺ), as distinct from all other branches of knowledge. Do you not see that he said, "The scholars are the heirs of the prophets," and the prophets left behind nothing but knowledge, and the knowledge of our Prophet (ﷺ) is his Sunnah. So whoever divests himself of knowledge of it is not among the heirs of the prophets.
